name: Saint Paul Miki and Companions
history: Twenty-six Catholics crucified on a hill outside Nagasaki on 5 February 1597, under the regent Toyotomi Hideyoshi. They included three Japanese Jesuits, six Franciscan friars from Spain, Mexico and India, and seventeen Japanese laymen, among them catechists, craftsmen and three boys. Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit and a gifted preacher, preached his last sermon from the cross and forgave his executioners.
life: Christianity had come to Japan with Saint Francis Xavier in 1549 and spread widely, but by the 1590s Hideyoshi had come to fear it. In December 1596 he ordered the arrest of friars and Christians in Kyoto and Osaka. Each had part of an ear cut off, and they were marched hundreds of miles through the winter to Nagasaki as a warning to others. Paul Miki, born around 1564 into a well-to-do family and educated by the Jesuits, was close to ordination. On the cross he told the crowd that he was Japanese and a Christian, and that he forgave the regent and all who had caused his death. The martyrs sang psalms and encouraged one another until they were killed with lances. Persecution followed for more than two centuries, yet when missionaries returned in the 1860s they found hidden Christians who had kept the faith in secret. The martyrs were canonised in 1862.
prayerTo: Saint Paul Miki and holy martyrs of Japan, you sang and forgave as you died on your crosses. Pray for the Church in Japan and for Christians who suffer for their faith today. Pray for me, that I may never be ashamed of Christ, and that I may forgive those who wrong me as freely as you forgave. Amen.
penance: Pray for persecuted Christians and give to a charity that supports them. Forgive one person today who has hurt you, naming them before God.
meditation: From the cross Paul Miki prayed for the men who had condemned him. Is there anyone you would find it impossible to pray for?
